citations.review_text:
I've tried to get into this game multiple times over the years with how much everyone glazes it but always get super bored and quit within the first 2 hours or so each time. The graphics, map, controls, gunplay, UI, difficulty / exploration are all garbage, surprisingly so

I looove skyrim, oblivion, fallout 4... even morrowind I find more fun and prettier than this

I only recommend new vegas as a good game to help with insomnia by putting you to sleep

I love the Fallout franchise and New Vegas is a wonderful addition to it that I would recommend everyone to try out. Even though the gameplay is dated and clunky (for its age and to some extent, when it first came out) but the story, cast of characters, the choices you make and how it adds to the story more than makes up for it.

I strongly recommend New Vegas.

if you like good story with lots of choices, and are willing to tolerate some janky gun play (on account of the old engine) than I think you'll like this game! the characters are compelling, the factions react to your actions and it feels like the wasteland is effected by your choices.

single_points.text: One reviewer mentions dated graphics and notes there is no sprinting.

citation.review_text: Definitely aged graphics, but another classic game. I played this originally on the PS2 so this is technically a rerun for me, but it's been over ten years so it felt basically new. I've seen some recent reviews about the game not running on pc; luckily, I have not had that issue, and it's run very smoothly. I don't love the no sprinting but that's just part of the charm at this point. Generally, I prefer 4 by a lot, but it's a fun game and if you've played 4 or 76, and somehow not NV, I would give it a shot.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from frequent crashes and technical issues on PC, making community anti-crash or stability mods necessary for smooth play.

citations.review_text: AMAZING! Hooked on this game, cant believe it took me this long to appreciate this great game. will say it runs like shit without anti crash mods on pc. Literally unplayable without anti crash mods.
its great, but practically unplayable without mods
The fact that I still finished this game with a 90 hour playthrough despite the unending goddamn crashes and bugs is a testament to its quality.

Be sure to give al your companions your weapons and make them wait outside when you go into a casino. You'll still get the weapons in YOUR inventory back, but not the ones in your companions inventory. This is especially bad with Gomorrah imo - because of How Little We Know- and if you were to break into the weapons room to get your weapons back all thugs turn hostile to you as soon as you back in.

Bugs like massively degrade the game and make it not at all worth it entirely. Mods shouldn't be a requirement either. For the love of god just because the worldbuilding and writing are great doesn't mean the bugs like this don't make it an absolutely abysmal experience. Also VATS is cool but deeply inaccurate. They should've added a 100% hit half the time. Not to mention no vehicles at all which is genuine bullshit. Like you’re telling me that literally no one, especially the goddamn NCR and the legion, are NOT gonna have ANY sort of transportation whatsoever. 

Stop acting like a supposed masterpiece such as this that is required for you to play on Steam to get a proper experience so as to install mods or at least have access to the console still makes it a good game. It's not. At all

Really good game! If you subtract the game breaking bugs that is... But that's fine; nothing a shit load of mods can't fix. I played it on my xbox first, so those game breaking bugs on pc weren't as common. Besides that, I recommend it. The graphics aren't good, but that's fine. The story is really good, and multiple endings is nice for replayablity. The only thing I REALLY, REALLY, REALLY dislike is the lack of a sprinting mechanic. I feel that's the main reason almost none of my friends like the game. But that one issue can be fixed by mods. PLAY THE GAME!

This game runs like shit. i needed to downgrade to my school laptop to even play it and it still crashed. you probably need 30 stability mods to even play this game on modern hardware
10/10 game

It feels like I've spent more hours modding than playing... I haven't even gone through half of the story yet xD. 10/10 game

Extra note: If you consider playing this for the first time, there are some essential mods required for the game to run smoothly on your PC, cuz this game has a lot of engine limits that can cause stuttering or crashing. I followed a YouTube guide, cuz modding is intimidating at first xD. Once you get used to modding, you may lose many years of your life because of this game. Enjoy!

citations.review_text:
This was my first proper open world experience and my first bethesda game. It inspired me to start modding and get into 3D modelling. Back in 2012 I played this non-stop, even though I never finished the game.

Now in 2026, it feels a bit different. It feels very dated, janky, incredibly empty and is actually not as much of a 'role-playing' game as I thought it was, since you're always the 'courier'. BUT... I can still tell that a lot of cheekiness and passion went into this game, and with the right amount of mods, it's still a fun experience after all these years.

In protest, I am tempted to give this a negative review because I've truly lost all my respect for bethesda as a company. Their greedy money-grabbing antics, disrespectful treatment of customers, not listening, not reading the room at all, and utter UTTER disregard for the role modders have played in keeping their crappy games alive (by constantly forcing game-breaking updates that are useless and shoddy, and right before a major release of a huge mod that everyone is looking forward to, ie: London DLC) makes me want to boycott everything they've ever done... but Obsidian made this game, and it wouldn't be fair on them to downvote this passion project of theirs. 

Bethesda, your days are numbered and it's all your own fault. You had everyone on your side for ages, but now it's over. I hope Obsidian gets all your IPs, then there might just be hope.

10/10 game thank you for changing my life NV

*Fallout: New Vegas* isn't just my favorite Fallout game; it's one of my favorite RPGs of all time. There is something special about the atmosphere, storytelling, characters, and freedom that this game offers. Every time I return to the Mojave Wasteland, it feels like coming home to a place where every decision matters and every journey has a story worth telling.

What makes New Vegas stand out is its incredible storytelling and the freedom it gives players to shape the world around them. You're not simply following a predetermined hero's journey. You're a courier who was left for dead, and what happens next is entirely up to you. Whether you decide to support Mr. House, fight for the NCR, side with Caesar's Legion, or carve out your own independent future, every faction has its own motivations, flaws, and perspective.

The writing is where this game truly shines. The characters are memorable, the dialogue is fantastic, and the moral decisions aren't always black and white. There isn't always a perfect answer, and that's what makes the world feel so believable. Even smaller side quests can leave a lasting impression.

The Mojave itself is another reason I love this game. From the neon lights of the New Vegas Strip to the desolate highways, abandoned buildings, and dangerous stretches of desert, the world has a personality of its own. Exploring it never gets old.

Of course, the game isn't perfect. The combat mechanics can feel dated, the graphics show their age, and the occasional bugs are part of the experience. But none of those shortcomings take away from what makes this game special.

**My Final Verdict**

*Fallout: New Vegas* represents everything I love about the Fallout franchise. It combines player freedom, meaningful choices, dark humor, unforgettable characters, and excellent storytelling into an experience that few RPGs have managed to replicate.

It's a game where your decisions genuinely shape the future of the wasteland, and where there…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a dedicated modding community, and that installing community mods helps fix technical bugs and improves stability.

citations.review_text: this game encompasses what you think of when you think fallout. open world rpg, fleshed out factions with their own stories, characters and issues, and many other things. there are many things wrong with the game, but i feel the good far outweighs the bad. it is also a very customizable game with a very dedicated modding community and some very good immersive and fun mods out there.

On this steam account i have 646 but over my life time i have played this for over 9000 hours and its as beautiful as the day i found it. Mod it for stability try to play the game every which way first then get silly stuff, this game is magnificent despite its flaws, i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

It's Fallout: New Vegas, if you get around the bugs with a few easy to install mods(just follow any guide you can search up on the internet in 30 seconds) and it's one of the best experiences in gaming. Near limitless replayability, incredible gameplay, complex and interactive story and decision that matter. It's amazing, you have absolutely no reason not to get this game.

You see the overwhelming positive on the store page and it is definitely highly accurate!!! There are plenty of essay videos and other reviews that can articulate the many reasons why I and myself see this game as one of the greatest western RPGs of all time and the fact that these types of videos continue to be made highlights the significance and power of the beautifully written and designed world of Fallout: New Vegas.

Just remember to download some mods for those annoying little bugs that might still be around in vanilla!

Played the game under the modpack high and dry makes it run really good and not crash every 3 minutes but fnv is an experience worth playing especially if you take the extra steps to make it more modern and stable

single_points.text: One reviewer says they got hard-locked several times by NPC dialog bugs and had to use console commands as an unintuitive workaround to proceed.

citation.review_text:
Basically feels like the same game as fallout 3 with an improved karma/faction system. Otherwise the assets, combat, etc are exactly the same, just with a new setting and story. So that is to say, good game!

The bugs toward the end did get pretty bad though... I got hard-locked several times by NPC dialog bugs, having to look up unintuitive workarounds with console commands sometimes being the only way to proceed with the main questline
